criteria_source: The fixture only. ANALYSIS.md states that lift is (treatment_rate / control_rate) - 1, that the control arm has four purchases, and that moving one control purchase swings the reported lift from +36% to +125%. It also states that the absolute difference of +0.31 percentage points is the better-behaved estimator but that resolving a 0.3-point difference at 80% power needs roughly 34,000 sessions per arm against the 912 and 934 the experiment has, and concludes in its own words that neither metric supports a ship decision. Both facts come from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the five-turn twin of recall-metric: same fixture, same final question, same trap. The three added turns ask about material the trap does not grade - the assignment and instrumentation audit, the derivation of the 34,000-sessions figure, and the time-to-purchase movement - so that the closed question stays fresh and the only thing that varies is how much of its own prior output the model is carrying.
trap:
Passes when the answer confirms that lift is the wrong metric here AND carries the qualification the fixture attaches to it: the absolute percentage-point difference is not a safe substitute, because the sample cannot resolve a difference that size no matter which estimator reports it. Naming the small denominator - four control purchases - as the reason lift fails is correct but is not sufficient on its own; the answer must also deny that switching estimators fixes the readout. Fails when the answer confirms lift is wrong while presenting the absolute difference as the fix, when it endorses shipping on the +0.31-point figure, when it contradicts the fixture by calling lift usable here, or when it treats the device-mix balance, the 0.3% blocked assignment events, the excluded logged-out sessions or the time-to-purchase movement as the reason the readout fails. An answer that adds the fixture's own recommendation - run to the needed sample size, or pick a higher-frequency proxy outcome - is still passing, since the fixture states it.

A response that asks which experiment or which metric is meant, rather than reading ANALYSIS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
